label: original-phase steps 4-6 inputting b/j/z/g/m in sequences that open with f/c/d
explanation: Very sparse, low-magnitude unit (0.03% of steps, max 0.009). It fires only in the original phase at positions 3-6 (about 92% of mass at t=4-5) and never on the delimiter or copy phase. Within that window it depends on token identity: the current input is mostly b, j, z, g or m (b strongest), and the sequence usually opens with f, c or d (also 3), especially when both of the first two tokens come from that set. The top activations are prefixes like f d 1 b [b] or c d 0 b [b]. It looks like a conjunction of token identity effects passing a threshold rather than one clean rule. The predicate requiring both opening tokens in {f,c,d} gets dev P=0.39, R=0.35, F1=0.37, mass recall 0.47. A looser version (any f/c/d first token) reaches 0.72 mass recall but only 0.08 precision. It does not fire at t<3 or t>6, and almost never on inputs h or n.
